title: Petrov's Defense
summary: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6: counterattack e4 instead of defending e5.
body:
The Petrov (also called the Russian Defense) answers 2.Nf3 with a symmetrical counterattack on e4. It's one of the most solid defenses in chess, but it has one big trap you must know.

The key rule:
- After **3.Nxe5**, play **3...d6 first**! Only after the knight retreats do you take on e4.
- 3...Nxe4? 4.Qe2! is bad for you: if the knight moves, Nc6+ discovers check and wins your queen.

Your plan:
- Get a solid, symmetrical position with active pieces.
- Your knight on e4 is a strong piece. Support it with **...d5** and **...Bd6** or **...Be7**.
- Castle quickly and use the open e-file.

Variations you'll meet:
- **3.Nxe5 d6 4.Nf3 Nxe4**: the classical main line.
- **3.d4**: White opens the center at once.
- **3.Nc3**: a Four Knights game.
- **4.Nxf7?!** (the Cochrane Gambit): take the knight and defend calmly.

lines.name: Classical: 3.Nxe5 d6
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 {Take your share of the center.} 2. Nf3 Nf6 {The Petrov: counterattack e4.} 3. Nxe5 d6 {The key move. Kick the knight first. Never 3...Nxe4? 4.Qe2!} 4. Nf3 Nxe4 {Now it's safe to take.} 5. d4 d5 {Support the e4 knight.} 6. Bd3 Nc6 {Develop and pressure d4.} 7. O-O Be7 {Prepare to castle.} 8. c4 Nb4 {Hit the d3 bishop. A main line of top-level chess.}
lines.explain: Your knight on e4 and solid center give you equality. Next: ...O-O, ...Be6 or ...Bf5.

lines.name: Five Knights: 5.Nc3
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Nxe5 d6 4. Nf3 Nxe4 5. Nc3 {White offers a knight trade and plans to castle queenside.} 5... Nxc3 {Trade knights.} 6. dxc3 Be7 {Develop and prepare to castle.} 7. Be3 O-O {Castle.} 8. Qd2 Nd7 {Solid development. If White castles long, play ...Nf6 and ...c5 or ...b5.}
lines.explain: White has quick development and may attack with O-O-O and h4. Keep calm, finish developing, and use ...Nf6 and ...Re8.

lines.name: 3.d4: the Steinitz attack
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. d4 {White opens the center.} 3... Nxe4 {Take the pawn.} 4. Bd3 d5 {Support the knight.} 5. Nxe5 Nd7 {Challenge the strong e5 knight.} 6. Nxd7 Bxd7 {Recapture and develop.} 7. O-O Bd6 {Active, natural development. Next: ...O-O and ...Qh4 or ...Re8 ideas.}
lines.explain: Your pieces are active and the position is symmetrical. Castle, then contest the e-file.

lines.name: Cochrane Gambit: 4.Nxf7
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Nxe5 d6 4. Nxf7 {The Cochrane Gambit: a piece for two pawns and an attack.} Kxf7 {Take the knight!} 5. d4 c5 {Counterattack the center. Next ...Nc6 and ...Kg8 to bring the king to safety.}
lines.explain: You are a piece up for two pawns. Hit the center with ...c5 and ...Nc6, tuck the king away, and your extra piece wins in the end.

lines.name: Four Knights: 3.Nc3
lines.pgn: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Nc3 {Defend e4: a Four Knights Game.} 3... Nc6 {Develop and defend e5.} 4. Bb5 Bb4 {Symmetry: the Four Knights Spanish.} 5. O-O O-O {Castle.} 6. d3 d6 {Solid and equal. Watch out for Bg5 pins; ...Bxc3 and ...Qe7 are typical.}
lines.explain: A calm, symmetrical position. Watch the pins on the f6 and f3 knights, and be ready to break with ...d5 when it's safe.
